newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa still critical, doctors delay test.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa still critical, doctors delay test.

text.p: Mother Teresa remained in critical condition in an Indian heart clinic on Thursday and doctors again delayed an X-ray test.
"Although Mother Teresa remains in critical condition, she appears to be a little better," doctors at Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said in a regular bulletin on her health.
"We are waiting for her heart condition to improve to be able to withstand an invasive procedure in the near future," the bulletin added.
"The condition of Mother Teresa is fluctuating," Dr Tarun Praharaj, one of her doctors said.
Praharaj said the doctors had delayed at least until Friday an angiography X-ray procedure to determine whether surgery was needed. "We may do it tomorrow or Sunday," he said.
The test uses an X-ray and an opaque dye injected into blood vessels to check for arterial blockage.
The 86-year-old nun had a peaceful night following chest pains and breathing problems on Wednesday.
Doctors told reporters Mother Teresa, who was admitted to hospital last Friday with an irregular heartbeat, appeared to be cheerful.
They said she ate a breakfast of porridge, cottage cheese and tea, and had soup and sandwiches for lunch.
There were indications that Mother Teresa required surgery, her cardiologist, Dr A.K. Bardhan, said.
"All indications lead to the conclusion that she has a blockage in her coronary artery," Bardhan said.
Mother Teresa had no chest pain for nearly five years after she last underwent heart surgery in 1993, Bardhan said.
"But what happened last Friday was serious heart failure and chest pain. Therefore angioplasty is almost certain. Let us see when the doctors can conduct the angiography," he added.
Mother Teresa, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work with the poor, was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989.
She has undergone coronary angiography twice -- in the United States in 1991 and at the Birla centre in 1993.
Each time she also had angioplasty, in which surgeons insert a balloon into an artery and inflate it to unblock the artery.
Mother Teresa was moved to the Birla centre on Tuesday from the nearby Woodlands Nursing Home.
Mother Teresa's heart problem later worsened and her doctors delayed the angiography, originally planned for Wednesday.
Meanwhile, members of the Missionaries of Charity, the religious order Mother Teresa founded in 1949, prayed for the recovery of the 1979 Nobel Peace prize winner.
"We are having prayers all over the world for her recovery," Sister Priscilla, the order's spokeswoman, said.
The charity, devoted to the poor, destitute and dying, has about 4,500 nuns in some 80 countries.
Britain's Independent newspaper reported on Wednesday that Mother Teresa had begged her doctors to let her die.
"She talked very openly about not wanting to live any longer," the Independent quoted Jim Towey, a former seminarian with Mother Teresa's Missionaries of Charity order, as saying.
"She's helped so many people to die that she can accept mortality much better than her doctors," Towey said.
